verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              विदार्य कर्णस्तां सेनां युधिष्ठिरमथाद्रवत् । रथहस्त्यश्वपत्तीनां सहस्त्रैः परिवारितः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Riving through that army Karna encountered the pious king surrounded by thousands of cars, elephants, horses and footsoldiers.

verses.sanskrit: नानायुधसहस्राणि प्रेरितान्यरिभिर्वृषः । छित्त्वा बाणशतैरुग्रैस्तानविध्यदसंभ्रमात् ॥२॥
verses.english: Sundering with hundreds of dreadful shafts the thousands of arms discharged at him by his enemies Karna fearlessly went through the army.

verses.sanskrit: निचकर्त शिरांस्येषां बाहूनूरूंश्च सूतजः । ते हता वसुधां पेतुर्भग्नाश्चान्ये विदुद्रुवुः ॥३॥
verses.english: The charioteer's son sundered the heads, the arms and the things of his enemies who, deprived of life, fell down on earth. Others, finding their division dispersed, took to their heels.

verses.sanskrit: द्राविडास्तु निषादास्तु पुनः सात्यकिचोदिताः । अभ्यद्रवज्जिघांसन्तः पत्तयः कर्णमाहवे ॥४॥
verses.english: The Dravida, the Andhaka and the Nishada infantry, excited by Satyaki once more rushed upon Karna with a view to kill him in that battle.

verses.sanskrit: ते विबाहुशिरस्त्राणाः प्रहताः कर्णसायकैः । पेतुः पृथिव्यां युगपच्छिन्नं शालवनं यथा ॥५॥
verses.english: Shorn of their arms and head-dresses and killed by Karna with his arrows they fell down all at once on earth like a forest of Sala trees cut down.

verses.sanskrit: एवं योधशतान्याजौ सहस्राण्ययुतानि च । हतानीयुर्महीं देहैर्यशसा पूरयन्दिशः ॥६॥
verses.english: Deprived of life and filling the heaven and earth with their fame, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands of warriors fell down with their bodies on earth.

verses.sanskrit: अथ वैकर्तनं कर्णं रणे क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम् । रुरुधुः पाण्डुपञ्चाला व्याधिं मन्त्रौषधैरिव ॥७॥
verses.english: The Pandus and Panchalas obstructed Karna, the son of Vikartana who proceeded in anger to battle like the destroyer himself even as people seek to obstruct a disease with incantations and drugs.

verses.sanskrit: स तान्प्रमृद्याभ्यपतत्पुनरेव युधिष्ठिरम् । मन्त्रौषधिक्रियातीतो व्याधिरत्युल्वणो यथा ॥८॥
verses.english: Grinding all those combatants Karna once more rushed upon Yudhishthira like irresistible disease unchecked by incantations, drugs and rites.

verses.sanskrit: स राजगृद्धिभी रुद्धः पाण्डुपञ्चालकेकयैः । नाशकत्तानतिक्रान्तुं मृत्युर्ब्रह्मविदो यथा ॥९॥
verses.english: Then obstructed by Pandus, Panchalas and Kekayas who were all desirous of rescuing the king he could not overcome them as Death cannot those conversant with Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: ततो युधिष्ठिरः कर्णमदूरस्थं निवारितम् । अब्रवीत्परवीरघ्नं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ॥१०॥
verses.english: Thereupon beholding Karna, the slayer of hostile heroes, obstructed at a distance, an Yudhishthira, with eyes reddened with anger, said-

verses.sanskrit: कर्ण कर्ण वृथादृष्टे सूतपुत्र वचः शृणु । सदा स्पर्धसि संग्रामे फाल्गुनेन तरस्विना ॥११॥
verses.english: O Karna, O son of a charioteer, O you of vain seeing, hear my words, You always challenge in fight Phalguna of quick speed. Abiding by the counsel of the son of Dhritarashtra you always obstruct us.

verses.sanskrit: तथास्मान्बाधसे नित्यं धार्तराष्ट्रमते स्थितः । यद्बलं यच्च ते वीर्यं प्रद्वेषो यस्तु पाण्डुषु ॥१२॥
verses.english: You bring all your strength, energy and hatred to bear upon the Pandus. Do you display today all your great manliness. I will today give battle and destroy your desire for fight.

verses.sanskrit: तत्सर्वं दर्शयस्वाद्य पौरुपं महदास्थितः । युद्धश्रद्धां च तेऽद्याहं विनेष्यामि महाहवे ॥१३॥
एवमुक्त्वा महाराज कर्णं पाण्डुसुतस्तदा । सुवर्णपुङ्खैर्दशभिर्विव्याधायस्मयैः शरैः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Having said this to Karna, the monarch, the son of Pandu, pierced him with ten arrows, made of iron and furnished with golden wings.

verses.sanskrit: तं सूतपुत्रो दशभिः प्रत्यविद्ध्यद‌रिन्दमः । वत्सदन्तैर्महेष्वासः प्रहसन्निव भारत ॥१५॥
verses.english: Then that Suta's son, the subduer of foes and a great bowman, pierced him in return as if smiling, O Bharata, with ten arrows furnished with heads like the calf's tooth.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽवज्ञाय तु निर्विद्धः सूतपुत्रेण मारिष । प्रजज्वाल ततः क्रोधाद्धविषेव हुताशनः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Thus placed by Suta's son in contempt the mighty-armed heroes was worked up with anger like fire with oblation.

verses.sanskrit: ज्वालामालापरिक्षिप्तो राज्ञो देहो व्यदृश्यत । युगान्ते दग्धुकामस्य संवर्ताग्नेरिवापरः ॥१७॥
verses.english: The body of Yudhishthira surrounded by the flames of anger looked as if it was second Samvartaka fire intended to burn the whole universe, in course of the great devastation (Pralaya).

verses.sanskrit: ततो विस्फार्य सुमहच्चापं हेमपरिष्कृतम् । समाधत्त शितं बाणं गिरीणामपि दारणम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then stretching his huge bow made of gold he set sharp arrows capable of breaking down the mountains.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पूर्णायतोत्कृष्टं यमदण्डनिभं शरम् । मुमोच त्वरितो राजा सूतपुत्रजिघांसया ॥१९॥
verses.english: With a view to kill the Suta's son he drew his bow to its fullest stretch and discharged that fatal shaft as the rod of the destroyer himself.

verses.sanskrit: स तु वेगवता मुक्तो बाणो वज्राशनिस्वनः । विवेश सहसा कर्णं सव्ये पार्श्वे महारथम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Discharged with great velocity and making a sound like that of a thunder bolt the arrow suddenly pierced the great car-warrior Karna on his left side.

verses.sanskrit: स तु तेन प्रहारेण पीडितः प्रमुमोह वै । स्रस्तगात्रो महाबाहुर्धनुरुत्सृज्य स्यन्दने ॥२१॥
verses.english: Greatly assailed by the violence of that spike the powerful Karna, with weaked limbs, swooned away on his car his bow dropping from his hand.

verses.sanskrit: गतासुरिव निश्चेताः शल्यस्याभिमुखोऽपतत् । राजापि भूयो नाजघ्ने कर्णं पार्थहितेप्सया ॥२२॥
verses.english: He fell down unconscious in front of Shalya as if he was dead. King Yudhishthira did not attack again on Karna by keeping in mind the interest of Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: ततो हाहाकृतं सर्वं धार्तराष्ट्रबलं महत् । विवर्णमुखभूयिष्ठं कर्णं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Seeing Karna in that state the huge army of Dhritarashtra's son exclaimed Oh! and alas! and the faces of all the warriors became pale.

verses.sanskrit: सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे क्ष्वेलाः किलकिलास्तथा । पाण्डवानां महाराज दृष्ट्वा राज्ञः पराक्रमम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: O monarch, witnessing the power of their king the Pandava army sent up leonine roars and cries of joy.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिलभ्य तु राधेयः संज्ञां नातिचिरादिव । दध्रे राजविनाशाय मनः क्रूरपराक्रमः ॥२५॥
verses.english: Regaining his sense in no time the dreadful son of Radha made up his mind to kill Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: स हेमविकृतं चापं विस्फार्य विजयं महत् । अवाकिरदमेयात्मा पाण्डवं निशितैः शरैः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Drawing his dreadful bow made of gold, Vijaya, the valiant son of Suta, began to resist Pandu's son with his sharp arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्षुराभ्यां पाञ्चाल्यौ चक्ररक्षौ महात्मनः । जघान चन्द्रदेवं च दण्डधारं च संयुगे ॥२७॥
verses.english: Then with two razor he killed in that battle Chandradeva and Dandadhara, the two Panchalas princes who guarded the wheels of the high-souled (Pandu king).

verses.sanskrit: तावुभौ धर्मराजस्य प्रवीरौ परिपार्श्वतः । रथाभ्याशे चकाशेते चन्द्रस्येव पुनर्वसू ॥२८॥
verses.english: Each of those heroes stood by Yudhishthira shining like the constellation Punarvasu by the side of the moon.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरः पुनः कर्णमविद्ध्यस्त्रिंशता शरैः । सुषेणं सत्यसेनं च त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरताडयत् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira again struck Karna with thirty arrows. He pierced Sushena and Satyasena each with three arrows.

verses.sanskrit: शल्यं नवत्या विव्याध त्रिसप्तत्या च सूतजम् । तांस्तस्य गोप्तॄन्विव्याध त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरजिह्मगैः ॥३०॥
verses.english: He pierced Shalya with ninty and struk Karna with seventy-three arrows. He also struck every one of Karna's body guards with three straight arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रहस्याधिरथिर्विधुन्वानः स कार्मुकम् । भित्त्वा भल्लेन राजानं विद्ध्वा षष्ट्याऽनद‌त्तदा ॥३१॥
verses.english: Then laughing and shaking his bow the son of Adhiratha wounded the king's body with a Bhalla, then pierce him with sixty arrows and then sent up a loud war-cry.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रवीराः पाण्डूनामभ्यधावन्नमर्षिताः । युधिष्ठिरं परीप्सन्तः कर्णमभ्यर्दयञ्छरैः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Then to rescue the king many leading Pandava warriors fell upon Karna in great anger and began to assail him with their arrows.

verses.sanskrit: सात्यकिश्चेकितानश्च युयुत्सुः पाण्ड्य एव च । धृष्टद्युम्नः शिखण्डी च द्रौपदेयाः प्रभद्रकाः ॥३३॥
यमौ च भीमसेनश्च शिशुपालस्य चात्मजः । कारूषा मत्स्यशेषाश्च केकयाः काशिकोसलाः ॥३४॥
verses.english: Satyaki, Chekitana, Yuyutshu, Shikhandin, the sons of Draupadi, the Prabhadrakas, the twins, Bhimasena, Shishupala, the Karushas, the Matsys, the Kaikeyas the Kashis and the Kosalas, all those valiant and highly active warriors assailed Vasushena.

verses.sanskrit: एते च त्वरिता वीरा वसुषेणमताडयन् । जनमेजयश्च पाञ्चाल्यः कर्णं विव्याध सायकैः ॥३५॥
वाराहकर्णनाराचैर्नालीकैर्निशितैः शरैः । वत्सदन्तैर्विपाठैश्च क्षुरप्रैश्चटकामुखैः ॥३६॥
verses.english: The Panchala prince Janamejaya then struck Karna with many arrows. Encircling Karna with a view to kill him they all rushed upon him with various arrows, such as boareared, Narachas, Nalika, Nishat, calf-toothed, Vipatha, razor shaped, with diverse other weapons chariots horses, elephants.

verses.sanskrit: नानाप्रहरणैश्चोग्रै रथहस्त्यश्वसादिभिः । सर्वतोऽभ्यद्रवत्कर्णं परिवार्य जिघांसया ॥३७॥
स पाण्डवानां प्रवरैः सर्वतः समभिद्रुतः । उदीरयन् ब्राह्ममस्त्रं शरैरापूरयन्दिशः ॥३८॥
verses.english: Thus assailed on all sides by the leading Pandava warriors Karna invoked the assistance of the Brahma weapon and filled all the quarters with his arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शरमहाज्वालो वीर्योष्मा कर्णपावकः । निर्दहन्पाण्डववनं वीरः पर्यचरद्रणे ॥३९॥
verses.english: Like burning fire having arrows for its scorching flame Karna fought on consuming that forest of Pandava troops.

verses.sanskrit: स सन्धाय महास्त्राणि महेष्वासा महामनाः । प्रहस्य पुरुषेन्द्रस्य शरैश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Aiming some powerful weapons and laughing the noble Karna, the great bowman, sundered the bow of that best of men, Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सन्धाय नवतिं निमेषान्नतपर्वणाम् । बिभेद कवचं राज्ञो रणे कर्णः शितैः शरैः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Thereupon aiming ninety straight arrows within the twinkling of an eye Karna cut-off, with those sharp arrows, the armour of his antagonist.

verses.sanskrit: तद्वर्म हेमविकृतं रत्नचित्रं बभौ पतत् । सविद्युदभ्रं सवितुः श्लिष्टं वातहतं यथा ॥४२॥
verses.english: Made of gold and set with jewels that armour looked beautiful as if it fell down like the cloud driven by the wind and smitten by the rays of the sun.

verses.sanskrit: तदङ्गात्पुरुषेन्द्रस्य भ्रष्टं वर्म व्यरोचत । रत्नैरलङ्कृतं चित्रैर्व्यभ्रं निशि यथा नभः ॥४३॥
verses.english: The armour, adorned with jewels fallen off the body of that foremost of men, appeared like the sky in the night bespangled with stars. Having his armour sundered with those arrows the son of Pritha covered with blood.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नवर्मा शरैः पार्थो रुधिरेण समुक्षितः । ततः सर्वायसीं शक्तिं चिक्षेपाधिरथिं प्रति ॥४४॥
verses.english: He hurled in anger at the son of Adhiratha a dart made of iron. He too cut of that (dart) shining in the sky with seven arrows; sundered with shafts by that great bowman it reached the earth.

verses.sanskrit: तां ज्वलन्तीमिवाकाशे शरैश्चिच्छेद सप्तभिः । सा छिन्ना भूमिमगमन्महेष्वासस्य सायकैः ॥४५॥
ततो बाह्वोर्लर्लाटे च हृदि चैव युधिष्ठिरः । चतुर्भिस्तोमरैः कर्णं ताडयित्वा नदन्मुदा ॥४६॥
verses.english: Then striking Karna with four lances on his two arms, forehead and chest Yudhishthira again and again sent up loud shouts.

verses.sanskrit: उद्भिन्नरुधिरः कर्णः क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन् । ध्वजं चिच्छेद भल्लेन त्रिभिर्विव्याध पाण्डवम् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Then blood gushed out from Karna wounds. Then filled with anger breathing like a snake he cut-off his enemy's standard and struck Pandava with three Bhallas. He also cutoff his two quivers and car into pieces.

verses.sanskrit: इषुधी चास्य चिच्छेद रथं च तिलशोऽच्छिनत् । कालवालास्तु ये पार्थं दन्तवर्णाऽवहन्हयाः ॥४८॥
तैर्युक्तं रथमास्थाय प्रायाद्राजा पराङ्मुखः । एवं पार्थोभ्युपायात्स निहतः पार्ष्णिसारथिः ॥४९॥
verses.english: Riding on the car drawn by horses white as teeth and having black hairs which used to bear Partha the king fled away from the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: अशक्नुवन्प्रमुखतः स्थातुं कर्णस्य दुर्मनाः । अभिद्रुत्य तु राधेयः पाण्डुपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥५०॥
verses.english: Unable to stand before Karna, thus did the son of Pritha, with his charioteer Parshin slain, cheerlessly fly away.

verses.sanskrit: वज्रच्छत्रांकुशैर्मत्स्यैर्ध्वजकूर्माम्बुजादिभिः । लक्षणैरुपपन्नेन पाण्डुना पाण्डुनन्दनम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: It seemed at the time when Karna, the son of Radha was chasing Yudhishthira as if he is intended to catch him forcibly so as to touch him on should with his fair colour hand having lucky marks as thunderbolt, umbrella, goad, fish, flag, tortoise and lotus etc. in order to attain purity. In the meantime, a memory of commitment he had made once before Kunti, chained his racing feet.

verses.sanskrit: पवित्रीकर्तुमात्मानं स्कन्धे संस्पृश्य पाणिना । ग्रहीतुमिच्छन्स बलात् कुन्तीवाक्यं च सोऽस्मरत् ॥५२॥
तं शल्यः प्राह मा कर्ण गृहीथाः पार्थिवोत्तमम् । गृहीतमात्रो हत्वा त्वां मा करिष्यति भस्मसात् ॥५३॥
verses.english: King Shalya in the meantime made Karna alert by saying-"O Karna! Don't' touch king Yudhishthira at all nonetheless you should burn in the fire erupted due to anger within him. You touch may cause of death for you.

verses.sanskrit: अब्रवीत्प्रहसन्राजन् कुत्सयन्निव पाण्डवम् । कथं नाम कुले जातः क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितः ॥५४॥
verses.english: O king, said, smiling and censuring the son of Pandu-"In what family are you born? You are to observe the duties of a Kshatriya. Why do you leave the battle-field in haste, to save your life? Methinks, you do not know the duties of a Kshatriya.

verses.sanskrit: प्रजह्यात्समरं भीतः प्राणान्रक्षन्महाहवे । न भवान् क्षत्रधर्मेषु कुशलो हीति मे मतिः ॥५५॥
ब्राह्मे बले भवान् युक्तः स्वाध्याये यज्ञकर्मणि । मा स्म युद्ध्यस्व कौन्तेय मा स्म वीरान्समासदः ॥५६॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, Endued with Brahma force, you are better fitted for the study of the Vedas and sacrificial rites.

verses.sanskrit: मा चैतानप्रियं ब्रूहि मा वै व्रज महारणम् ॥५७॥
verses.english: Do not, O son of Kunti, fight again. Do not approach heroes and use harsh words towards them and do not go to great battles.”

verses.sanskrit: वक्तव्या मारिषान्ये तु न वक्तव्यास्तु मादृशाः । मादृशान्विब्रुवन्युद्धे एतदन्यच्च लप्स्यसे । स्वगृहं गच्छ कौन्तेय यत्र तौ केशवार्जुनौ ॥५८॥
न हि त्वां समरे राजन् हन्यात्कर्णः कथञ्चन । एवमुक्त्वा ततः पार्थं विसृज्य च महाबलः ॥५९॥
verses.english: This and another pains you would have to bear for inflicting harsh words upon the people like me. Hence, O son of Kunti, either go back to your home or march only in company of Sri Krishna and Arjuna. "O king! Karna will not slaughter you in battle-field."

verses.sanskrit: न्यहनत्पाण्डवीं सेनां वज्रहस्त इवासुरीम् । ततोपायाद्द्रुतं राजन्व्रीडन्निव नरेश्वरः ॥६०॥
verses.english: Having said this and left off the son of Pritha the highly powerful Karna began to slay Pandava like the holder of thunder-bolt, the army of Asuras.

verses.sanskrit: अथापयति राजानं मत्वान्वीयुस्तमच्युतम् । चेदिपाण्डवपञ्चालाः सात्यकिश्च महारथः ॥६१॥
verses.english: Then the king Yudhishthira, O king, took to his heels quickly in great shame. Seeing the king take to his heels, the Chedis, the Pandavas, the Panchalas and the powerful carwarrior Satyaki, the heroic sons of Draupadi and the twin sons of Madri followed him of eternal glory.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदेयास्तथा शूरा माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ । ततो युधिष्ठिरानीकं दृष्ट्वा कर्णः पराङ्मुखम् ॥६२॥
कुरुभिः सहितो वीरः प्रहृष्टः पृष्ठतोऽन्वगात् । भेरीशङ्खमृदंगानां कार्मुकाणां च निःस्वनः ॥६३॥
verses.english: Thereupon beholding the retreat of the army of Yudhishthira the heroes pursued them in great delight.

verses.sanskrit: बभूव धार्तराष्ट्राणां सिंहनादरवस्तथा । युधिष्ठिरस्तु कौरव्य रथमारुह्य सत्वरम् ॥६४॥
verses.english: Then there arose the leonine shout of the sons of Dhritarashtra accompanied by the sound of bugles, conch, mridangas and the twang of bows.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतकीर्तेर्महाराज दृष्टवान्कर्णविक्रमम् । काल्यमानं बलं दृष्ट्वा धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः ॥६५॥
verses.english: O king, his horses become tired so getting upon quickly the car of Srutakirti, Yudhishthira began to witness the prowess of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: स्वान् योधानब्रवीत्कुद्धो निघ्नतैतान् किमासतः । ततो राज्ञाऽभ्यनुज्ञाताः पाण्डवानां महारथाः ॥६६॥
verses.english: Then beholding his own army slain the pious king Yudhishthira said to his own warriors-"Kill them; why do you sit idle?"

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनमुखाः सर्वे पुत्रांस्ते प्रत्युपाद्रवन् । अभवत्तुमुलः शब्दो योधानां तत्र भारत ॥६७॥
verses.english: Thereupon obtaining the command of the king all the mighty car-warriors of the Pandavas headed by Bhimasena rushed upon your sons.

verses.sanskrit: रथहस्त्यश्वपत्तीनां शस्त्राणां च ततस्ततः । उत्तिष्ठत प्रहरत प्रैताभिपततेति च ॥६८॥
verses.english: O Bharata, then there arose a great tumult of the warriors, chariots, elephants, horses, infantry and weapons.

verses.sanskrit: इति ब्रुवाणा ह्यन्योन्यं जघ्नुर्योधा महारणे । अभ्रच्छायेव तत्रासीच्छरवृष्टिभिरम्बरे ॥६९॥
verses.english: “Rise, strike, face the foe" uttering those words the warriors killed one another in that great battle.

verses.sanskrit: समावृतैर्नरवरैर्निघ्नद्भिरितरेतरम् । विपताकध्वजच्छत्रा व्यश्वसूतायुधा रणे ॥७०॥
verses.english: On account of the showers of arrows discharged by them a shadow as that of clouds seemed to spread over the field abounding in the best of men killing those weaker then they.

verses.sanskrit: व्यङ्गाङ्गावयवाः पेतुः क्षितौ क्षीणाः क्षितीश्वराः । प्रवणादिव शैलानां शिखराणि द्विपोत्तमाः ॥७१॥
verses.english: Deprived of their standards, flags, umbrellas, horses, drivers, weapons, armas and other limbs, the kings, weakened, fell down on earth.

verses.sanskrit: सारोहा निहताः पेतुर्वज्रभिन्ना इवाद्रयः । छिन्नभिन्नविपर्यस्तैर्वर्मालङ्कारभूषणैः ॥७२॥
verses.english: Resembling mountain summits, the best of elephants with their drivers slain, fell down like mountains clapped by thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit: सारोहास्तुरगाः पेतुर्हतवीराः सहस्रशः । विप्रविद्धायुधाश्चैव विरथाश्च रथैर्हताः ॥७३॥
verses.english: With their armours and other equipments torn and shattered thousands of horses and warriors fell down.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिवीरैश्च संमर्दे पत्तिसंघाः सहस्रशः । विशालायतताम्राक्षैः पद्मेन्दुसदृशाननैः ॥७४॥
verses.english: The earth is strewn with the heads of the kings who never come back from the battlefield, having expansive coppery eyes and faces like the full moon.

verses.sanskrit: शिरोभिर्युद्धशौण्डानां सर्वतः संवृता मही । यथा भुवि तथा व्योम्नि निःस्वनं शुश्रुवुर्जनाः ॥७५॥
verses.english: The earth was covered all over with heads of heroes, dreadful in battle, with expansive coppery eyes and with faces resembling the lotus or the moon. People heard on the earth as well as in the sky noise proceeding, from the singing and music of the band of Apsaras going in celestial cars.

verses.sanskrit: विमानैरप्सरः सङ्घैर्गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः । हतानभिमुखान्वीरान् वीरैः शतसहस्रशः ॥७६॥
आरोप्यारोप्य गच्छन्ति विमानेष्वप्सरोगणाः । तद्दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं प्रत्यक्षं स्वर्गलिप्सया ॥७७॥
verses.english: Having placed on their cars thousands of heroes slain in battle the Apsara went on.

verses.sanskrit: प्रहृष्टमनसः शूराः क्षिप्रं जघ्नुः परस्परम् । रथिनो रथिभिः सार्धं चित्रं युयुधुराहवे ॥७८॥
verses.english: Beholding that wonderful spectacle the heroes, desirous of attaining to heaven, quickly and delightedly killed one another.

verses.sanskrit: पत्तयः पत्तिभिर्नागाः सह नागैर्हयैर्हयाः । एवं प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे गज-वाजि-नरक्षये ॥७९॥
verses.english: In that battle the car-warriors fought wondrously with car-warriors, the infantry with infantry, the elephants with elephants and horses with horses.

verses.sanskrit: सैन्येन रजसा वृत्ते स्वे स्वाञ्जघ्नुः परे परान् । कचाकचि युद्धमासीद्दन्तादन्ति नखानखि ॥८०॥
verses.english: When the battle, destructive of elephants, horses and men, thus raged on the field was enshrouded with dust raised by the troops; the enemies then killed enemies and friends killed friends.

verses.sanskrit: मुष्टियुद्धं नियुद्धं च देहपाप्मासुनाशनम् । तथा वर्तति संग्रामे गज-वाजि-नरक्षये ॥८१॥
verses.english: Then there took place a skirmish destructive of life and sins-the warriors dragging one another by their locks, biting one another with their teeth, tearing one another with their nails and striking one another with their clenched fists and fighting with one another with bare arms.

verses.sanskrit: नराश्वनागदेहेभ्यः प्रसृता लोहितापगा । गजाश्वनरदेहान्सा व्युवाह पतितान्बहून् ॥८२॥
verses.english: As that battle, destructive of elephants, horses and men, raged on fiercely a river of blood flew from the bodies of men, horses and elephants. That stream carried away many bodies of men, horses and elephants that fell there.

verses.sanskrit: नराश्व-गजसम्बाधे नराश्व-गज-सादिनाम् । लोहितोदा महाघोरा मांसशोणितकर्दमा ॥८३॥
verses.english: In that huge army abounding in men, horses and elephants, the river, formed by the blood of men, horses and elephants, became miry with flesh and that highly terrible river, striking terror into the timid, carried away the bodies of men, horses and elephants.

verses.sanskrit: नराश्वगजदेहानां वहन्ती भीरुभीषणा । तस्याः पारमपारं च व्रजन्ति विजयैषिणः ॥८४॥
गाधेन चोत्प्लवन्तश्च निमज्ज्योन्मज्य चापरे । ते तु लोहितदिग्धाङ्गा रक्तवर्मायुधाम्बराः ॥८५॥
verses.english: Some, desirous of victory, crossed it. Some plunged into its depths and some rose above its surface.

verses.sanskrit: सस्रुस्तस्यां पपुश्चास्यां मम्लुश्च भरतर्षभ । रथानश्वान्नरान्नागानायुधाभरणानि च ॥८६॥
verses.english: Their limbs, weapons and robes became all besmeared with blood. O foremost of Bharatas, some bathed in it, some drank its liquid.

verses.sanskrit: वसनान्यथ वर्माणि वध्यमानान् हतानपि । भूमिं खं द्यां दिशश्चैव प्रायः पश्याम लोहितम् ॥८७॥
verses.english: We saw the cars, horses, men, elephants, armours, ornaments, robes, coats of mail, earth, sky and heaven and all directions were all seen dyed in red colour.

verses.sanskrit: लोहितस्य तु गन्धेन स्पर्शेन च रसेन च । रूपेण चातिरक्तेन शब्देन च विसर्पता ॥८८॥
verses.english: With the smell, the touch, the taste, the exceedingly redness of the blood and its gushing sound almost of the warriors became very cheerless.

verses.sanskrit: विषादः सुमहानासीत्प्रायः सैन्यस्य भारत । तत्तु विप्रहतं सैन्यं भीमसेनमुखास्तदा ॥८९॥
verses.english: The Pandava heroes headed by Bhimasena and Satyaki again attacked fiercely on Kaurava's army already destroyed in its considerable fraction.

verses.sanskrit: भूयः समाद्रवन्वीराः सात्यकिप्रमुखास्तदा । तेषामापततां वेगमविषह्यं निरीक्ष्य च ॥९०॥
verses.english: Beholding the irrepressible force of their attack, the army of your sons, O king, turned their back.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्राणां ते महासैन्यमासीद्राजन् पराङ्मुखम् । तत्प्रकीर्णरथाश्वेभं नरवाजिसमाकुलम् ॥९१॥
verses.english: With armours and coats of mail, displaced, weapons and bows loosened from their hands, your army, abounding in cars, horses, elephants and men, fled away in all directions, being agitated by the enemy as a herd of elephants in the forest is afflicted by lions.

verses.sanskrit: विध्वस्तवर्मकवचं प्रविद्धायुधकार्मुकम् । व्यद्रवत्तावकं सैन्यं लोड्यमानं समंततः । सिंहार्दितमिवारण्ये यथा गजकुलं तथा ॥९२॥
